statement.p: (b) What does your answer to part (a) tell you about \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r where C is the circle (x-20)^2+(y-25)^2=1 in the xy-plane, oriented clockwise?
(c) If C is any closed curve, what can you say about \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r?

(d) Now let C be the half circle (x-20)^2+(y-25)^2=1 in the xy-plane with y > 25, traversed from (21, 25) to (19, 25). Find \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r by using your result from (c) and considering C plus the line segment connecting the endpoints of C.

static.solution:
(a) Let \vec F=\left(6z+6x^{4}\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}+\left(3y+2z+2\sin\mathopen{}\left(y^{4}\right)\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+\left(6x+2y+3e^{z^{4}}\right)\,\mathit{\vec k}. Then \mbox{curl }\vec F = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} \amp \frac{\partial}{\partial y} \amp \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ 6(z + x^{4}) \amp 3 y + 2(z + sin(y^{4})) \ \amp 6 x + 2 y + 3 e^{z^{4}} \end{array} \right| = \vec 0.
(b) Since C is a closed curve, \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r=0 by Stokes' Theorem.
(c) The line integral is 0 for any closed curve C in 3-space.
(d) Let C_1 be the line segment from (19, 25) to (21, 25). Then, by (c), we know \int_{C + C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{C}\vec F\cdot d\vec r + \int_{C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = 0. Thus \int_{C}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = -\int_{C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r. On C_1, we have 19\le x\le 21, y = 25 and z = 0, so \int_{C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{19}^{21}\,0 + 6 x^{4}\,dx = \frac{6}{5}\,x^{5}\bigg|_{19}^{21} = \frac{9648012}{5}. Thus \int_{C}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = -\frac{9648012}{5}.
